uncited: It builds on [Chunk Visibility Culling](5031-chunk-visibility-culling.md) by adding a distance-based sort to the visible set, ensuring correct depth ordering for transparent or blended rendering passes.

It differs from [Octree Frustum Culling & LOD Selection](5771-octree-frustum-culling-lod-selection.md) by operating on flat chunk lists rather than hierarchical tree traversal, and from [Out-of-Core Frustum Clipping](6688-out-of-core-frustum-clipping.md) by not performing geometric clipping of chunk geometry, only visibility culling.
**Inputs:** Camera view and projection matrices; list of active chunks; camera world position.
**Change Detection:** If the camera chunk position has changed since the last frame (compared against `m_LastCamChunkPos`), proceed to rebuild the ordered list.
**Distance Sorting:** Sort the visible chunks by distance from the camera.
*   **Precision:** Using squared distance avoids precision issues with square roots but may lead to ties for chunks at the same horizontal distance.
**Time Complexity:** $O(N \log N)$ for sorting $N$ visible chunks.
**Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ to store the list of visible chunks.
**Strengths:** Simple to implement; ensures correct rendering order for transparent chunks.

**Limitations:** Ignores Y-axis distance, which may cause incorrect sorting for vertically stacked chunks; recalculates full sort on chunk change, which may be inefficient if chunk changes are frequent but minor.
**When to use:** When transparent chunk rendering requires strict back-to-front or front-to-back ordering and chunks are primarily distributed horizontally.
**When not to use:** When vertical sorting is critical or when chunk visibility changes frequently without camera movement.
It is used in real-time voxel rendering systems to manage chunk visibility and rendering order.
